summary: Okta externalId casefold collision maps CLI sessions to incorrect service account, blocking runner and Grafana access
description: Issue summary: After the Okta attribute deprecation change rolled out to identity-proxy (2026-03-09), some CLI SSO-authenticated sessions are resolving to the wrong service account. Impact: Engineers lose access to internal-runner and Grafana dashboards; workflows that trigger model evals via support CLI fail. Environment: production in us-west; affects self-hosted and Dedicated customers' internal tooling integrations. Observed behavior: When a user's Okta externalId differs only by case from an existing service account (e.g., 'svc-Eval' vs 'SVC-eval'), identity-proxy's casefolding normalization collapses them to a single key and maps sessions to the first-match service account. Expected behavior: ExternalId should be matched case-sensitively for service-account resolution, or a clear collision detection should surface and reject ambiguous mappings.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create two Okta service accounts with externalId="svc-Eval" and externalId="SVC-eval".
2) Deploy identity-proxy with the 2026-03-09 attribute-deprecation behavior (casefold normalization).
3) Authenticate via support-cli using SSO; exchange token for a session tied to 'svc-Eval' identity.
4) Observe session subject in authz logs and Grafana role mapping; note that some sessions are mapped to the other service account intermittently under load.
logs: Auth trace samples: authz.trace_id=trc-20260310-7a9c, auth.log: "resolved_subject=service-account:svc-eval (id=sa-1024)" then later "resolved_subject=service-account:svc-eval (id=sa-2048)" for different requests. Splunk search: https://splunk.redwood.internal/en-US/app/search/search?q=authz.trace_id%3Dtrc-20260310-7a9c (internal). Identity-proxy container logs: last-deploy commit abc123def, config flag okta.casefolding=true.
investigation_notes:
- First-pass: correlation between the 2026-03-09 deploy and onset of incidents.
- Hypothesis: okta-sync pipeline now normalizes externalId to lower-case (casefold) to align with Okta deprecation changes; this introduced non-unique keys when service accounts differ only by case.
- Repro on staging with the same config reproduced ambiguous mapping under concurrent requests; race due to in-memory map insertion order.
- Related commit: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy@abc123 (okta attribute deprecation).
- Quick mitigation: toggled okta.casefolding=false in identity-proxy rollout to restore prior behavior; affected sessions began resolving consistently to expected identities (temporary).
- Long-term: require a migration plan to either enforce canonical externalId uniqueness (case-insensitive) or maintain case-sensitive exact-match behavior for service-account resolution and add collision detection to sync pipeline.

resolution: Mitigation applied: set okta.casefolding=false in identity-proxy to restore case-sensitive resolution as a stopgap. Next steps: merge PR that adds explicit collision detection, a fatal error on ambiguous externalId mapping for service accounts, and a migration script to canonicalize or rename colliding service accounts. Estimated patch release: 2026-03-14. Follow-up owner: Oliver Grant.
